**2026-10-31.** A patch release with two `llm` transport fixes, both found on a real phone line: OpenAI audio
models can now give a JSON answer, and a failed model call logs the provider's reason. There is no
`urn:sutra:q:1.0` change, no archive format, deploymentId or snapshot change, and no migration.

## Fixed

- **OpenAI audio models failed every call that asked for JSON.** The `openai` adapter sent
  `response_format: {type: json_object}` (Chat Completions; `text.format` on Responses) to every
  model. The audio chat models (`gpt-audio…`, `gpt-4o-audio-preview`, any model id containing
  `audio`) refuse it with HTTP 400 "Invalid parameter: 'response_format' of type 'json_object' is
  not supported with this model." A channel with `require: [audio-understanding, json-output]`
  picked such a model, so every call failed. For these models JSON is now asked for in the system
  text (*Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else.*) and no `response_format` is sent;
  the transport parses the answer. They still declare `json-output`, so `require: [json-output]`
  still selects them.
- **The JSON modes refused a request that never said "JSON".** OpenAI's JSON mode returns HTTP 400 when no message mentions JSON. When a call has `json: true` and neither its
  system text nor any message says "JSON", the `openai` adapter now adds the same instruction to
  the system text and still sends `response_format`. A request that already says JSON is sent as
  before.
- **A JSON answer inside prose was not parsed.** A model asked for JSON in words often answers
  with the JSON in a fenced block between sentences. The reply's `json` is now read from the first
  ` ```json ` (or bare ` ``` `) block when the whole answer is not JSON; a block in another
  language is not taken.
- **A failed model call did not log why.** A failed sync `llm` call logged only
  `SUTRA.DISPATCH.INSTANCE_FAILED` / `SUTRA.LLM.CALL.FAILED`, even at `debug`; a permanent failure
  (a 4xx) was not logged at all, so with the admin API off the provider's reason was nowhere. Now,
  for sync, async (outbox), job and channel-handle calls:
  - each failed candidate attempt is logged at `WARN` (`llm candidate failed: <reason>`) with
    `channel`, `provider`, `model`, `candidate`, `class`, `http_status`, `provider_code` and
    `fall_back`;
  - the call's failure is logged at `WARN` (`llm call failed: <diagnostic>`) with the same fields,
    `trace_id` and, when the engine stamped it, `instance`, under `code=SUTRA.LLM.CALL.FAILED` —
    the `cause_code` of the instance-failed line, so one search finds both;
  - the reason (HTTP status, the provider's error code, its message on one line cut to 300
    characters) is in the diagnostic the engine stores with a failed instance or a dead-lettered
    start, with `http_status` and `provider_code` attributes, instead of the raw error body.

  URLs in a reason have their query values and credentials redacted (`redact_url`), and the
  candidate's key is replaced wherever a provider echoes it; it is replaced in the failure detail
  before anything else sees it. Prompts and answers are never logged.

## Changed

- The `examples/ai-summarize` stub model server refuses `response_format` for an audio model and a
  JSON-mode request that never says "json", as the real API does, and answers an audio model asked
  for JSON in words with a fenced block in prose.
- `examples/ai-advanced` has a `hear-json` flow (audio in, a parsed JSON answer out, on an OpenAI
  audio model); `live-check.sh` checks it on `gpt-audio` (`OPENAI_AUDIO_MODEL` overrides).

## Security

- `tools/sutra-vscode`: `minimatch` under `vscode-languageclient` raised from 5.1.9 to 11.0.3 with
  an npm override (CVE-2026-118764, denial of service through a crafted glob; no
  `vscode-languageclient` release takes a fixed `minimatch`). The client only uses its
  `Minimatch` class, which 11 still exports. Extension tests 72/72, build green.
- The engine image's new glibc finding, CVE-2026-84243 (message-catalog lookup through the
  `LANGUAGE` variable), has no Debian fix and is not reachable: the engine never calls
  `setlocale`, so it runs in the C locale, and the base image has no locale data. It is triaged in
  `.trivyignore.yaml` with the other base-image entries (re-triage on 2026-11-09).

Tests: tier-1 `audio_model_json_is_asked_in_words_not_response_format`,
`json_mode_adds_the_word_json_when_the_request_never_says_it` (sutra-llm-openai);
`a_fenced_answer_in_prose_yields_json`, `failed_inline_call_logs_its_reason_without_secrets`,
`failed_async_call_logs_its_reason_and_redacts_an_echoed_key` and the `failure_reason` unit tests
(sutra-transport-llm); tier-2 `tc_ai_advanced_audio_understanding_json_answer` (the stub refuses
`response_format` for the audio model, so it passes only when JSON is asked in words).

## Upgrading

- Nothing to do: no configuration, archive, snapshot or `q:` change. A channel that already asks an
  OpenAI audio model for JSON starts working; a reply that used to carry `jsonError` for a JSON
  answer wrapped in prose now carries `json`.
- A JSON-mode call whose prompt never says "JSON" gets one more sentence in its system text.
- Log pipelines that match `llm candidate failed` now see it for permanent failures too, with the
  reason in the message; the failure diagnostic's message carries the parsed reason instead of the
  raw provider error body.
